paragraphs: Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat.

His father, Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, was very dear to Rav, as in Bava Batra 8b, where Rav applied to him the verse "and those who lead the many to righteousness shall be like the stars forever and ever."

Hyman writes that his son Rav Yehudah, apparently, also merited to receive from Rav; although Hyman does not find anywhere that he spoke with him face to face, he does find in several places that he said teachings in Rav's name, as in Berakhot 47a, 48a; Shabbat 30b, 118b (and the same attribution should be corrected at 119b), 153a; Eruvin 14b, 96a; Sukkah 46b; Taanit 14a, 29b; Megillah 5a; Moed Katan 16a; Yevamot 64b; Menachot 35b. And he disagrees with Rav Yehudah in Taanit 14a. Rav Huna bar Chinena said to him, "Thus said Rav Chisda," as in Moed Katan 16a; and in Eruvin 14b, Rav Yosef said Rav Yehudah said Shmuel said — Rav Rachumi taught thus: Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said; and it implies that this refers to what precedes, that Rav Yosef said it in his name. He is also mentioned in Eruvin 85b and Yoma 76b.

notes.text: The notice retains both Shabbat118b and119b. Its proposed attribution correction at119b is not a replacement of118b.

The consulted Shabbat 118b directly names Yehudah son of Shmuel bar Shilat reporting Rav. Hyman’s proposed attribution correction at 119b remains separate from that 118b occurrence; his tentative personal contact and absence of a recorded face-to-face exchange remain his argument.
